short_definition: A rogue Wi-Fi access point masquerading as a legitimate network to steal connected users' data.
layman_explanation: Setting up a fake Wi-Fi router named 'Airport_Free_WiFi' across from the real airport router to intercept traffic.

short_definition: Tricking a mobile carrier into porting a target's phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM card.
layman_explanation: Pretending to be you at a phone store so all your phone calls and 2FA text messages go to a scammer's phone.

short_definition: The modern Wi-Fi Protected Access security protocol offering improved encryption and brute-force protection.
layman_explanation: The modern security standard that keeps your home Wi-Fi encrypted and safe from password-guessing tools.

short_definition: An unauthorized wireless access point connected to a secure corporate network without administrative approval.
layman_explanation: An employee secretly plugging a cheap home Wi-Fi router into an office Ethernet jack, creating a backdoor.

short_definition: Searching for unsecured Wi-Fi wireless networks while moving around in a vehicle.
layman_explanation: Driving around neighborhoods with a laptop to map open or weakly protected Wi-Fi connections.

short_definition: Sending unsolicited messages to nearby Bluetooth-enabled devices without authorization.
layman_explanation: Beaming unwanted pop-up text messages or pictures to someone's phone over Bluetooth in a crowded train.

short_definition: Gaining unauthorized access to information on a wireless device through a Bluetooth connection.
layman_explanation: Secretly stealing photos, contacts, and text messages from a phone using a Bluetooth exploit.

short_definition: Sending forged deauthentication frames to kick connected devices off a Wi-Fi network.
layman_explanation: Sending fake disconnect signals to trick your phone into disconnecting from your home Wi-Fi.

short_definition: A Web page presented to newly connected Wi-Fi users before granting full internet access.
layman_explanation: The hotel or coffee shop web screen asking you to enter your room number or agree to terms before connecting.

short_definition: Using specialized hardware to trick nearby devices into connecting to a rogue access point automatically.
layman_explanation: A gadget that shouts 'I am your saved home Wi-Fi!' so your phone automatically connects to it.

short_definition: Exploiting weak 8-digit PINs in Wi-Fi Protected Setup to recover the main network password.
layman_explanation: Brute-forcing a simple 8-digit PIN on the back of a router to bypass a long Wi-Fi password.

short_definition: Key Reinstallation Attacks exploiting flaws in the WPA2 4-way handshake to decrypt Wi-Fi traffic.
layman_explanation: A flaw in older Wi-Fi security that lets hackers eavesdrop on encrypted Wi-Fi traffic without knowing the password.

short_definition: Configuring a wireless router to suppress or broadcast its network name (SSID).
layman_explanation: Turning off your Wi-Fi network's name sign so neighbors don't see it listed on their phones.

short_definition: Flooding radio frequencies with noise signal to disrupt wireless communications.
layman_explanation: Blaring a deafening siren on the same frequency as a walkie-talkie so no one can hear the conversation.

short_definition: A security exploit where infected USB charging stations steal data or install malware on connected phones.
layman_explanation: Plugging your phone into a public airport charging kiosk that secretly steals your photos while charging.

short_definition: A cellular eavesdropping device that acts as a fake cell tower to intercept calls and location data.
layman_explanation: A fake cell tower that tricks nearby phones into connecting to it so operators can intercept calls and texts.

short_definition: Altering sender contact details in text messages to make texts appear to originate from trusted brands.
layman_explanation: Making a scam text message show up directly inside your official bank's text thread on your phone.

short_definition: Exploiting vulnerabilities in a smartphone's underlying cellular radio modem chip.
layman_explanation: Hacking the internal radio chip that manages cellular calls, bypassing the main phone operating system.

short_definition: Intercepting or relaying Near Field Communication signals used for contactless payments.
layman_explanation: Relaying contactless payment signals from a card in your pocket to a reader miles away.

short_definition: Circumventing Wi-Fi router access controls by cloning an approved device's MAC address.
layman_explanation: Copying an approved device's physical hardware number to sneak onto a restricted Wi-Fi network.

short_definition: Impersonating trusted BLE devices like smart locks or fitness trackers to send unauthorized commands.
layman_explanation: Tricking a smart door lock into thinking your phone is the owner's phone to unlock a door.

short_definition: A Wi-Fi setting preventing connected devices from communicating directly with each other on the same network.
layman_explanation: Preventing hotel guests on the same Wi-Fi network from seeing or connecting to each other's laptops.

short_definition: A legacy, broken Wi-Fi security protocol that can be cracked in minutes using basic tools.
layman_explanation: An obsolete 1990s Wi-Fi security standard that is easily cracked today.

short_definition: A Wi-Fi security mode requiring individual username and password authentication via a RADIUS server.
layman_explanation: Enterprise Wi-Fi where every employee logs in with their own personal credentials rather than a shared password.

short_definition: Installing mobile applications from third-party sources outside official app stores.
layman_explanation: Downloading an app file directly from a website instead of getting it safely from Apple's App Store or Google Play.

short_definition: Removing built-in software restrictions on mobile operating systems to gain full root access.
layman_explanation: Unlocking your phone's software to bypass manufacturer safety restrictions.

short_definition: Malicious mobile apps designed to intercept 2FA SMS messages and overlay fake bank screens.
layman_explanation: A malicious phone app that displays a fake login screen over your real banking app to steal your password.

short_definition: A sophisticated zero-click mobile spyware suite capable of silently reading messages and activating cameras.
layman_explanation: Advanced spyware that infects smartphones through invisible zero-click messages, recording calls and location.

short_definition: A mobile vulnerability requiring zero interaction from the target victim to execute payload code.
layman_explanation: A malicious message that infects your phone the moment it arrives, without you ever opening or tapping it.

short_definition: A mobile attack where a malicious app draws a transparent window on top of legitimate applications.
layman_explanation: Placing an invisible fake login window on top of your legitimate app to steal typed passwords.

short_definition: Analyzing broadcast beacon frames sent by routers to discover network configurations.
layman_explanation: Eavesdropping on public radio announcements sent by Wi-Fi routers to learn network details.

short_definition: Devices constantly broadcasting names of previously connected Wi-Fi networks in search of access points.
layman_explanation: Your phone constantly shouting out the names of your home and workplace Wi-Fi networks looking for connections.

short_definition: Using portable automated devices to capture WPA Wi-Fi authentication handshakes for offline cracking.
layman_explanation: A portable pocket gadget that collects encrypted Wi-Fi handshakes to crack passwords later.

short_definition: Flaws in global telecommunication routing protocols allowing attackers to redirect calls and texts.
layman_explanation: Flaws in global cell carrier networks that let attackers redirect your SMS text messages and phone calls.

short_definition: Vulnerabilities in 4G/5G signaling protocols enabling subscriber tracking and denial of service.
layman_explanation: Exploiting 4G/5G cell network management messages to track phone locations remotely.

short_definition: Setting up unauthorized mini cell towers to intercept mobile calls and cellular data locally.
layman_explanation: Setting up a mini cellular tower in an office building to eavesdrop on nearby mobile phones.

short_definition: An OS security mechanism isolating mobile apps so they cannot access other apps' data without permission.
layman_explanation: Keeping every app in its own isolated room so a game app cannot read your private WhatsApp chats.

short_definition: Tracking a physical device's location by observing its MAC address and Wi-Fi probe requests across retail sensors.
layman_explanation: Stores tracking your movement across a mall by monitoring your smartphone's Wi-Fi signals.

short_definition: Extending the physical range of Bluetooth signals to unlock cars or doors remotely while the key is far away.
layman_explanation: Relaying the signal from your car key inside your house to unlock your car sitting in the driveway.

short_definition: Flaws in wireless file-sharing protocols that leak partial hashes of phone numbers and email addresses.
layman_explanation: Wireless file-sharing features accidentally broadcasting scrambled versions of your phone number to nearby strangers.

short_definition: Security mechanisms measuring exact signal travel time to prevent relay attacks on smart keys.
layman_explanation: Measuring the exact nanosecond speed of light to ensure a digital car key is physically nearby.

short_definition: Secure authentication protocols used in enterprise Wi-Fi networks to encapsulate user logins in TLS tunnels.
layman_explanation: Sending your corporate Wi-Fi login details through an encrypted tunnel so network administrators can't read them.

short_definition: Impersonating legitimate 5G cell towers to downgrade devices to insecure 2G connections.
layman_explanation: Tricking your 5G phone into connecting to an old, unencrypted 2G network to intercept calls.

short_definition: Extracting secret cryptographic keys from a physical SIM card to copy it onto a duplicate blank card.
layman_explanation: Physically copying the cryptographic chip inside your SIM card to create a twin duplicate card.

short_definition: A malicious custom keyboard app that logs every character typed across all applications.
layman_explanation: Downloading a decorative custom keyboard app that records every password and message you type.

short_definition: Security flaws in peer-to-peer Wi-Fi connection protocols allowing unauthorized file access.
layman_explanation: Flaws in peer-to-peer Wi-Fi connections that let nearby devices access your photos without permission.

short_definition: Using handheld radio scanners to steal data wirelessly from credit cards or passports.
layman_explanation: Scanning credit card details through your wallet using a hidden radio scanner as you walk past.
